title: Contractive substitution of bounded tuples in restricted series

source.place: Conrad, Several approaches to non-archimedean geometry, Exercise 1.2.8(3), PDF p.7; norm-at-most-one specialization with contractivity. Local archival copy WANTED; read https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/aws.pdf online 2026-10-24.

proof.text: Put $T=T_r(F)$ and let $P\subseteq T$ be the $F$-linear subspace of finite-support coefficient families, that is, polynomials. By [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion], the Gauss norm is finite, separates points, satisfies the ultrametric inequality and $\|fg\|\le\|f\|\|g\|$, and total-degree truncations converge to every $f\in T$. In particular $P$ is dense. The coefficient formula also gives $\|cf\|=|c|\|f\|$: for $c=0$ both sides vanish, and for $c\ne0$ multiplication by the positive real number $|c|$ commutes with the finite-valued supremum of the bounded coefficient values. Thus $T$ is a normed $F$-vector space with the Gauss metric, and $P$ has its induced norm. These assertions include $r=0$, with one coefficient and $T=P=F$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dense-subspace-contractive-extension] with base field $F$, ambient vector space $E=T$, dense subspace $D=P$, complete target vector space $B$ and map $u$. The hypotheses on the norm of $B$ imply the ordinary triangle inequality as well as $\|cv\|=|c|\|v\|$; completeness and separation are assumed. Step 1 gives the required normed domain and density; step 2 gives the linear contraction. The cited statement requires no completeness of the domain. Obtain a continuous $F$-linear map $v:T\to B$, equal to $u$ on $P$, with $\|v(f)\|\le\|f\|$ for every $f$. In particular it preserves the unit and scalar map and sends $x_i$ to $b_i$.

proof.text:
It remains to check multiplication. For $f,g\in T$, write $p_N,q_N$ for their total-degree truncations. They converge to $f,g$, and $\|p_N\|\le\|f\|$. The product bound of [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] gives
$$\|p_Nq_N-fg\|\le\max(\|p_N\|\|q_N-g\|,\|p_N-f\|\|g\|)\longrightarrow0.$$
By linearity and contractivity of $v$, $v(p_Nq_N)\to v(fg)$. Likewise the assumed product bound in $B$ gives
$$\|v(p_N)v(q_N)-v(f)v(g)\|\le\max(\|f\|\|q_N-g\|,\|p_N-f\|\|g\|)\longrightarrow0.$$
Step 2 gives $v(p_Nq_N)=v(p_N)v(q_N)$. The ultrametric inequality applied to the difference of the two proposed limits bounds its norm by the maximum of these two errors, hence by every positive real number. Its norm is zero, so $v(fg)=v(f)v(g)$. Thus $v$ is a continuous $F$-algebra homomorphism.

u:|c_
u|\ge\epsilon/2\}$ finite. If $E\supseteq E_0$, every coefficient of $f-p_E$ has absolute value smaller than $\epsilon/2$, so $\|f-p_E\|\le\epsilon/2<\epsilon$. Thus the whole finite-subset net $p_E$ converges to $f$. By step 3,

Its limit is therefore exactly $v(f)$, so defining $\operatorname{sub}_b$ by the net gives the homomorphism already constructed and its contraction bound.

proof.text: If $w:T\to B$ is another continuous $F$-algebra homomorphism with $w(x_i)=b_i$, finite expansion of polynomials gives $w(p)=u(p)=v(p)$ on $P$. For the total-degree truncations of step 1, continuity gives $w(p_N)\to w(f)$ and $v(p_N)\to v(f)$. The same difference-of-limits norm argument as in step 4 gives $w(f)=v(f)$. Hence the continuous homomorphism is unique. For $r=0$, $\mathbf N^0$ has one element, the monomial is the empty product $1$, and $T_0(F)=F$. Every finite-subset net is eventually its single constant term; the constructed map is $c\mapsto c1_B$, as asserted.

Source: I read Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 1.2.8(3)-(4) (printed p.7) from the online PDF, converted to text; there is no local copy, and it is WANTED. Part (3) is bijectivity of Hom(T_n,A) with tuples of power-bounded elements. The item is its ‖b_i‖≤1 case plus contractivity, which is exactly what the citer lem-per-tate-rational-local-coordinates uses to recentre the polydisc. Step 1 takes norm, separation, product bound and truncation density from lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion and proves homogeneity inline. Step 2 is finite polynomial evaluation, with ‖b^ν‖≤1. Step 3 applies the Mathlib leaf lem-sfb-dense-subspace-contractive-extension (extendOfNorm); every hypothesis is matched, and B's completeness, homogeneity and separation are assumed. Step 4: multiplicativity follows from the two displayed error estimates, which I checked algebraically. Step 5: the full finite-subset net converges, using an ε/2 exceptional set. Step 6: uniqueness by density, continuity and separation; r=0 holds. Edge cases checked: r=0, b_i=1 (not topologically nilpotent), b_i=0, B with nilpotents; B=0 is excluded by ‖1‖=1 and separation. No duplicate in the DAG (rg -L over restricted series, Tate, substitution, Gauss). Batch-5 flag: gauss-completion is generic Gauss-norm analysis whose closure is only def-trf-restricted-series-presentation plus a Mathlib BoundedContinuousFunction leaf. It is not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality and is not given by them, so the citation stands. tool_uses entry for that node accepted: no node of the unit gives these analytic properties.
